newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura cuts back equities staff numbers in Osaka.
newsitem.headline: Nomura cuts back equities staff numbers in Osaka.

text.p: Broking giant Nomura Securities has cut the number of its equities staff in Osaka by more than a quarter and the move may prompt other brokerages to follow suit, industry officials said on Thursday.
A Nomura official said the number of staff in the section had been reduced to 33 from 45 in the past month by moving personnel to other Nomura offices.

"Japan's 'Big Bang' deregulation of markets will signal fierce competition among brokers in terms of cost performance. And it seems like we had more than enough people in the past," said Keiichiro Tsuchiya, manager of equities at Nomura's Osaka branch.

Brokers said the move was also partly due to the Osaka Securities Exchange's (OSE) decision to allow dealers in Tokyo to trade in new individual stock options to be offered in Osaka. These are scheduled to start trading on July 18 in both cities.
Osaka has benefited from the listing here of giants such as Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT), Matsushita Electric Industrial and Nintendo.

"There would be less need for a dealer in Osaka when they can place orders from Tokyo. This trend of shifting operations to Tokyo may get stronger," said Akihiro Shiroeda, a senior trader at Sanyo Securities.
"Times have changed as the bourse itself is now saying you could do deals from Tokyo," said a source at a foreign brokerage. "A while ago they were persuading us to keep our offices here."
Many foreign brokers opened shop in Osaka only for the purpose of trading in derivatives. Nikkei 225 futures are listed on the OSE.
Twenty-four foreign brokerages are members of the OSE, compared to 21 on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).

But PaineWebber shut down its securities operation in Osaka in March, saying it would focus its business in Japan on bonds and Citicorp Securities and HSBC James Capel Securities shut down their derivatives-trading operations in the city in January.
Among major Japanese brokerages, officials at Nikko Securities and Daiwa Securities said they had no immediate plans for major reshuffles in their Osaka equities operations.
The firms are next due to announce personnel plans in August and July respectively.
OSE President Kyoji Kitamura told Reuters that Osaka hoped to remain Japan's centre for derivatives trading.
"Traders will chose for themselves which exchange is more user-friendly, and we hope to provide that service," he said.
A trader at Nomura who is leaving Osaka, said that it used to be thought that an Osaka office was necessary in case of an earthquake in Tokyo.
"These days, the company's need to rationalise its business is obviously superseding that factor."
